evidence: Evra-Kaufman Remark 3.4 gives C0=1/(3(d+2)2^(d+3)), C1=(d+2)2^(d+2), bar-epsilon=(1/3)(beta/C1)^d, and mu=(C0(beta/C1)^d)^(2^(d+1)); at d=3 this is C0=1/960 and C1=160.

For every relevant positive-dimensional proper link, choose a minimum-weight vertex v. Its 0-cochain class has norm w(v) <= 1/2, while Lemma 2.3 gives ||delta{v}||=||Gamma^1({v})||=2w(v); therefore Exp_b^0 <= 2 and any uniform beta in the criterion satisfies beta <= 2.
Substitution gives bar-epsilon <= 1/1536000 and mu <= (1/491520000)^16 < 1e-139; epsilon=min(1/Q,mu) is therefore far below 0.08.
The conclusion is explicitly limited to the published EK closed-form route and does not rule out a 0.08 bound by other methods.

correctness.summary: The method-specific impossibility bound for the published Evra-Kaufman constants at d=3 is correct.

originality.summary: The EK paper supplies the general constants but does not appear to record the d=3 beta<=2 substitution or the resulting impossibility versus 0.08. The contribution is therefore a method-feasibility observation built from published formulas, not a new expansion theorem.

scientific_value.summary: The record prevents an impossible certificate target from being pursued with the published EK constants and cleanly separates that obstruction from the still-open possibility of proving the underlying expansion bound by another route.

limitations: Only the constants in the published Evra-Kaufman criterion are ruled out; re-optimized constants or different local-to-global theorems are not.
The beta<=2 observation is elementary and may be implicit in general coboundary-expansion folklore even though no explicit use of it for this d=3 threshold was located.
